story:
In a certain paint workshop, the colorist follows one unbreakable habit. Take any two pigments at all — call the first crimson and the second ochre.

She pours ochre into ochre and sets the result aside as Batch 1.

However she chooses her two starting pigments, crimson itself and Batch 1 always come out the exact same color. That is simply how this workshop works, without exception.

One morning her apprentice wonders about something. Take any pigment — again call it crimson. Pour crimson into crimson and set the result aside as Batch 1.

In this workshop, must crimson itself and Batch 1 always come out the same color?
